description.from:
Adopt the best retrieval techniques from Cerebras's knowledge-base writeup (https://www.cerebras.ai/blog/how-we-built-our-knowledge-base) into the Papyrus knowledge-query engine, without violating our cost model.

Full design doc: `docs/knowledge-retrieval-roadmap.md` (read it first — it contains verified current-state facts with file:line references). Background on the current retrieval path: `docs/internal-knowledge-research.md`.

## Strategy

Papyrus retrieval today is embedding-only (S3 Vectors, OpenAI text-embedding-3-small, 1536-dim). Cerebras's core lesson — never trust a single retrieval technique; run several and fuse the ranked lists — is the one we haven't absorbed. This matters acutely for threat intelligence: CVE IDs, hashes, actor aliases, and domains are exact tokens that embeddings blur.

## Hard constraints (non-negotiable)

1. **Scale to zero.** No provisioned-capacity services, no always-on components, no fixed monthly floors. Everything pay-per-use. This is why OpenSearch is disqualified (~$350/month floor × N instances).
2. **Fleet of single-publication instances, NOT multi-tenant.** Each Papyrus installation is one publication with its own stack. Never introduce tenant awareness. The economics: many instances run simultaneously, almost all idle.
3. **The knowledge-query Lambda is stdlib-only.** `amplify/functions/knowledge-query/resource.ts` bundles by copying `src/papyrus_knowledge_query` verbatim with an intentionally empty requirements.txt. Python 3.12, ARM64, 512 MB. No new pip dependencies in anything the Lambda imports.

## Epic sequencing

Priority order: (1) domain-scoring cleanup, (2) hybrid lexical + RRF, (3) age decay, (4) scope bundles, (5) distillation, (6) contextual chunks + gating, (7) MCP primitives, (8) rerank.

Dependencies: contextual-chunks is blocked by hybrid-lexical (needs its IDF/document-frequency table) and by distillation (both change embedding input — batch into ONE corpus re-embed). MCP primitives and rerank are blocked by hybrid-lexical. Age decay, scope bundles, and the scoring cleanup are independent and good first assignments.

**Rebuild coupling:** age decay, distillation, and contextual chunks all mutate vector metadata or embedding input. Batch into at most two index rebuilds: age-decay metadata can ride along with any sync; distillation + contextual chunks share one full re-embed (cost: dollars, not hundreds, at current corpus size).

## For implementers

- Verify every file:line reference before editing — they were verified 2026-07-19 and drift.
- Tests live in `procedures/newsroom/tests/` (see `test_knowledge_query.py`). Add tests with every change.
- Local smoke: `PYTHONPATH=src python -m papyrus_newsroom knowledge-query --query "..." --format structured --execution local` (see docs/internal-knowledge-research.md for full CLI usage and required env vars).
- Repo-visible content constraint: keep examples generic (CVE IDs, hashes, domains); no ransomware/exfiltration/key-leak themed examples.
description.to:
Adopt the best retrieval techniques from Cerebras's published knowledge-base architecture into the Papyrus knowledge-query engine, without violating our cost model.

**Primary source**: Cerebras Engineering, "How We Built Our Knowledge Base" (Isaac Tai, Daniel Kim, Mike Gao, July 2026) — https://www.cerebras.ai/blog/how-we-built-our-knowledge-base

**Full design doc**: `docs/knowledge-retrieval-roadmap.md` — per-idea integration designs with verified file:line references, dependency graph, and the rejected-alternatives analysis. Background on the current retrieval path: `docs/internal-knowledge-research.md`.

## What Cerebras built, and why it matters to us

Cerebras runs an internal knowledge base answering 15,000+ questions/day over data extracted from where it already lives (Slack, wikis, code, incident systems) rather than forcing a single-source-of-truth platform. Their pipeline: per-source connectors → LLM distillation into normalized artifacts → embeddings in one shared table (pgvector) → **multiple retrievers run in parallel** (full-text, vector, IDF-weighted, recency-decayed) → reciprocal rank fusion (RRF, k=60) → small-LLM rerank → synthesis with citations. Interfaces: a full planner→executor→synthesis pipeline for their web UI, and bare LLM-free retrieval primitives over MCP so any agent can orchestrate its own loop.

Their core lesson, and the one Papyrus has not absorbed: **never trust a single retrieval technique.** Full-text catches exact tokens that embeddings blur (pasted error strings, IDs); embeddings catch paraphrase; IDF separates rare-token signal from filler; age decay expires stale answers. Each retriever produces its own ranked list and the lists are fused — consensus across retrievers beats a strong showing in any one.

## Where Papyrus stands

**Already as good or better than Cerebras**: curation gating (only human-accepted references become evidence — they have nothing like this, and it doubles as our cost governor), knowledge-graph expansion, quality-aware ranking profiles, token-budgeted context packs per consumer profile, versioned knowledge lineage.

**The gap**: Papyrus retrieval is embedding-only (OpenAI text-embedding-3-small → AWS S3 Vectors, 1536-dim cosine). For a threat-intelligence publication this is the worst possible single-retriever choice of weakness: CVE IDs, file hashes, actor aliases, domains, and ATT&CK technique IDs are exactly the exact-token queries embeddings blur. A query for a literal CVE ID is served today purely by semantic similarity. There is also no recency signal (dates aren't even in vector metadata), no rank fusion, no rerank, no contextual chunk prefixes, no signal gating on what enters the index — and two latent defects: passage scoring still carries hardcoded boosts tuned for a prior AI/ML-research corpus, and an 8-chunk cap means only the first ~1,440 words of long reports are semantically searchable.

## The eight epics (each is self-contained; read its brief before starting)

1. **Passage-scoring cleanup** — retire corpus-specific boosts, extend heading boosts for threat-intel report structure, fix the token regex. Small, independent, good calibration assignment.
2. **Hybrid lexical (BM25) + RRF fusion** — the anchor investment. Pure-Python inverted-index artifact in S3, built during the existing vector-sync pass, fused with vector results at query time. Three other epics stack on it.
3. **Age decay** — dates into vector metadata + a small recency component in ranking. Tie-breaker, not dominator.
4. **Named scope bundles** — Cerebras's "projects," adapted: named filter bundles within one publication instance, defaulted per desk/procedure.
5. **Reference distillation** — LLM-extracted entity artifact per accepted reference (CVEs, actors, malware families, IOCs) embedded in place of raw composite text, with filterable entity metadata. Cerebras's biggest accuracy win.
6. **Contextual chunk embeddings + gating** — prepend title/source/date/section to embedded chunks (Anthropic contextual retrieval), gate low-signal chunks, lift the 8-chunk cap.
7. **MCP retrieval primitives** — LLM-free search tools external agents can orchestrate, mirroring Cerebras's MCP design.
8. **Eval-gated rerank + context expansion** — last on purpose; only recurring per-query LLM cost in the roadmap; ships only if the eval harness proves a win.

## What we are deliberately NOT copying

Ingest-everything (our curation gate stays), Socket-Mode real-time ingestion (our cadence is editorial), per-user defaults (ours are per-desk/procedure), and every piece of always-on infrastructure their enterprise scale amortizes.

## Hard constraints (non-negotiable)

1. **Scale to zero.** No provisioned-capacity services, no always-on components, no fixed monthly floors. Everything pay-per-use. This is why OpenSearch is disqualified (~$350/month floor × N instances).
2. **Fleet of single-publication instances, NOT multi-tenant.** Each Papyrus installation is one publication with its own stack. Never introduce tenant awareness. The economics: many instances run simultaneously, almost all idle.
3. **The knowledge-query Lambda is stdlib-only.** `amplify/functions/knowledge-query/resource.ts` bundles by copying `src/papyrus_knowledge_query` verbatim with an intentionally empty requirements.txt. Python 3.12, ARM64, 512 MB. No new pip dependencies in anything the Lambda imports.

## Epic sequencing and dependencies

Priority order: (1) scoring cleanup, (2) hybrid lexical + RRF, (3) age decay, (4) scope bundles, (5) distillation, (6) contextual chunks, (7) MCP primitives, (8) rerank.

Dependencies: contextual-chunks is blocked by hybrid-lexical (needs its IDF/document-frequency table) and by distillation (both change embedding input — batch into ONE corpus re-embed). MCP primitives and rerank are blocked by hybrid-lexical. Age decay, scope bundles, and the scoring cleanup are independent and good first assignments.

**Rebuild coupling:** age decay, distillation, and contextual chunks all mutate vector metadata or embedding input. Batch into at most two index rebuilds: age-decay metadata can ride along with any sync; distillation + contextual chunks share one full re-embed (cost: dollars, not hundreds, at current corpus size).
